summary: All four round-1 minors are correctly addressed. (1) The null/blank entryStepId guard is present in redirectExecution (Engine L235-238): fast no-op WARN before any CAS, preventing silent drift into the broken-cursor terminal-fail branch. (2) The dispatch-side duplicate success log is demoted to log.debug (FunnelEventService L263); the engine's LOG_REDIRECT info at L258 remains the single authoritative success record. (3) The findFirst()-safe comment is added in FunnelTriggerServiceImpl (L153-155), explaining uniqueness via the partial index. (4) The security guard comment is added before the LOG_DISPATCH_NO_MATCHED_ELEMENT warn (FunnelEventService L311-314). No behavioral regressions detected. The test improvements (FunnelEventServiceIT allowReEnter test strengthened with real terminal predecessor, new FunnelEventServiceTest drift-guard unit test) are correct and add coverage. One new minor observation on log-constant reuse.

new_findings.issue: The null/blank entryStepId guard emits LOG_REDIRECT_CLAIM_LOST (value: FUNNEL_REDIRECT_CLAIM_LOST), whose class-level comment documents it as 'lost claim-CAS no-op (sweep owns the row)'. The null/blank case fires before any CAS attempt — it is a dispatch precondition failure, not a sweep-race. An operator grepping FUNNEL_REDIRECT_CLAIM_LOST cannot distinguish the two causes. The inline comment in redirectExecution explains the distinction well, but the constant's semantic scope is now wider than its documentation.
new_findings.fix: Optionally introduce a dedicated constant such as LOG_REDIRECT_NULL_ENTRY (value: FUNNEL_REDIRECT_NULL_ENTRY_STEP) for the precondition guard, keeping LOG_REDIRECT_CLAIM_LOST strictly for the CAS-loss path. Alternatively, update the class-level LOG_REDIRECT_CLAIM_LOST comment to document both uses. Either makes the signal unambiguous in log aggregators.
